sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r8/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 25 (#24 grading_wiring_is_structurally_correct); Internal Quality Checks row 25 (legacy annotation: reward.toml/pinned judge/valid aggregate); Deterministic Checks rows for check-rubric-schema.py, check-scoring-policy.py, check-required-files.py, check-no-trialforge-judge-keys.py (read in memory via openpyxl read_only)
evidence: Parsed every file with tomllib in memory. scoring.toml lines 1-11: [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2 (sum 1.0); [floors] functional=0.05 -- equal to the template scoring.toml and the staged contract; every name has a directory (tests/gates/render, tests/gates/constraints, tests/scored/functional|polish|visual). All five judge.toml: [judge] judge="claude-code" (matches REWARDKIT_JUDGE in task.toml [verifier.env]), mode="batched", isolated=false, prompt_template="prompt.md"; no model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight keys; top-level keys only judge/scoring/criterion (no trialforge keys). Each declares [[judge.mcp_servers]] name="playwright" command="playwright-mcp" args [--headless,--isolated,--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium,--no-sandbox] (Dockerfile installs @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and symlinks /usr/local/bin/chromium). Only scored/functional/judge.toml lines 14-18 declare name="verifier" command="/usr/local/bin/python3" args=["/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py","$APP_RESTART_HELPER"], identical to template; test.sh line 193 `export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh"` after heredoc+sed generation and chmod 755, before run_suite; test.sh and restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to the frozen template; restart_mcp.py exposes single-use restart_app (.used marker). Functional prompt line 1/51 directs the judge to call restart_app once at protocol D and forbids shell. Suites: gates/render (1 criterion hro_gate_render) and gates/constraints (1 criterion hro_gate_shared) are aggregation=all_pass, type binary, weight 1.0, timeout 600 each; scored/functional 43 criteria, all binary, unique ids/names, weights 0.5-2.5 (sum 58.5), weighted_mean, timeout 9000; scored/polish 5 binary criteria weights 1.5-3 (sum 12), weighted_mean, timeout 900; scored/visual 5 likert criteria points=5 weight 1.2 each, weighted_mean, timeout 900. All descriptions non-empty; no unexpected criterion keys. Prompts resolve: each prompt.md exists beside its judge.toml, contains {criteria} and {app_context} (the only placeholders), and opens http://localhost:3000; test.sh lines 196-201 substitute {app_context} into /tests/*/*/prompt.md from tests/app_context.md. Budgets nest: gates 600+600 < 1500 suite budget, scored 9000+900+900=10800 < 11100, 1500+11100=12600 < verifier 13200 (task.toml). Adversarial probes: wiring is app-independent; a broken app cannot exploit it (gates are binary all_pass with zero weight; floor functional=0.05 in scoring.toml). A conforming alternative app is not disadvantaged by any structural element (no route/selector wiring). Run evidence: raw-evidence-index.json states full configured grading is absent; only scripted golden observations (with a real restart via the helper path, not via RewardKit MCP) exist. So actual RewardKit loading of these TOMLs and MCP $APP_RESTART_HELPER expansion are NOT EXERCISED for this candidate; the structural wiring is identical to the unchanged template, so this row's structural verdict does not depend on it. Missing full-run evidence is owned by the runtime/workload rows, not waived here.
